issues.title: review comments from Carl W
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
From: Carl Wallace Subject: [Rats] Review of draft-novak-rats-tacra-01
Archived-At: 
 <https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/rats/D7Z6QKWcz86n0STfF9AacUCKVMA>

I have reviewed both draft-novak-rats-tacra-01 and (briefly) draft-novak-lamps-tacra-est. I think TACRA seems like a good avenue to explore but the current draft buries the lede. Some comments on draft-novak-rats-tacra-01 are below.

```

issues.title: rework introduction, motivation
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
1) Most of the abstract and the introduction seem off topic. The entire "RUP" concept could be dropped from this draft. The third paragraph in the abstract is the closest to describing the work of the draft (plus the architecture theme in the second paragraph). Sharpening the focus on the API exercised by the attester would greatly improve the draft. As described here, today a "RUP" is an entity that an attester authenticates to using some credential. This draft defines a means for the attester to obtain credentials whose issuance process has been bolstered by remote attestation. That the RP is unaware of the details of the attestation-related information that is exchanged between the attester and the credential issuer is no more relevant than an RP that is unaware what certificate management protocol is used today. One would never refer to an EST-unaware Relying Party. 
	
```

issues.title: would issued credential include information that is actionable?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
2) Is there any consideration of whether the issued credential may include information that a RATS-aware Relying Party could act on (without disturbing the RATS-unaware RPs)? For example, in work that I do, the certificate policy OID included in an issued certificate varies based on presentation of attestation evidence. The sentence "while its clients and servers do not notice anything different" would be better as "while its clients and servers need not notice anything different".
```

issues.title: split out requirements
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
3) Given this draft is a set of requirements and the beginnings of an ecosystem of specifications, would it be best to split the requirements out into a separate draft? This would allow the requirements to proceed independent of the API and API instantiations (and may better align with the TWI SIG's publications of a requirements document). 
```

issues.title: simplify architecture diagram
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```

4) The architecture diagram in Figure 1 in Section 4.3 is very difficult to make sense of and is probably just too busy. For example, I can't tell where key generation would occur, but it looks to be on an arrow. The end of that arrow is Credential Authority, which would seem to be an EST server (where EST is used) but the CAS server box above appears to be labeled as an EST server. Prose clarifies that key generation is a Platform ABI function, though. Why does the CAS contact the Verifier? Oughtn't Verifier interactions be driven by the Secret Vault and Credential Authority?
```

issues.title: design goal 1: proof
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
5) Re: design goal 1, how does an attester prove that it should be able to retrieve a given set of credentials or cause issuance of new credentials for a given name?
```

issues.title: different mechanism for different awarenesses?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
7) Should design goal 5 account for using different mechanisms based on whether or not the target is RATS aware (or is RATS awareness being abstracted away by credential type details)? Does it matter if the credential that is returned is used more broadly than the requested target? Is there any concern about requesting new credentials per target when reuse is possible? Should this draft address key lifetime concepts, like rotation, deletion, revocation, etc.?
```

issues.title: is secret vault an implementation detail?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
8) Re: design goal 7, is the "secret vault" an implementation detail of the CAS? Likewise, for verifiers and credential authorities. If so, I'd drop this design goal. 
```

issues.title: goal 9 SHOULD/ is supporting many credeentials wrong?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
9) Re: design goal 9, this should be a SHOULD. Also design goal 2's requirement to support "most" credential formats is inconsistent with this one.

```

issues.title: how does trust flow?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
13) In general, the draft would benefit from describing how trust moves in the architecture, i.e., how do the attester, Secret Vault, and Credential Authority establish trust in the CAS, how do the Secret Vault and Credential Authority trust the Verifier, etc.
```

pulls.title: Resolve CSR/CEK-to-Evidence binding; add channel-binding security consideration
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
As discussed on the RATS list (my feedback of 12 September) and for the Tuesday CCC TWI SIG, this resolves the open binding TODOs and adds the channel-binding consideration. It is a proposal; happy to adjust normative strength or wording.

**What changed**

- New subsection *Binding Credential Keys to Evidence* (`{#binding}`): a concrete, verifiable construction for the CSR/CEKpub-to-Evidence binding — a collision-resistant digest of the CSR (Enrollment) or of CEKpub (Retrieval) placed in the Evidence freshness input together with the Freshness Handle, recomputed and checked by the Credential Authority / Secret Vault. It also states the three platform shapes the Platform Plug-in must handle: direct-in-report, nested via a vTPM quote where a paravisor owns the field, and provider-scoped where a fleet key masks the machine. Resolves the TBD on the Enrollment bullet and the TODOs on the Enroll-/Retrieve-Credential parameters.
- New Security Considerations subsection *Binding Evidence to the Credential-Acquisition Channel* (`{#channel-binding}`): the binding above ties the CSR/CEKpub to the platform and to freshness, but not to the channel; over the untrusted CAS conduit a relay can obtain a credential unless the exchange also binds a value derived from the channel's shared secret (the RFC 9266 TLS exporter). Also resolves the CAS-client-authentication TODO with a pointer to that value.
- Adds RFC 9266, ID-Crisis (ASIA CCS 2026), and Intra-handshake.fail (CVE-2026-33697) to informative references.

**Grounding (measured, reproducible)**

The enrollment construction is verified end-to-end on AMD SEV-SNP: a worked example builds the CSR in the guest, binds `REPORT_DATA = SHA-512(nonce || CSR)`, and a verifier checks the report and its VCEK chain to ARK-Milan (from the AMD KDS) plus the CSR proof of possession. The three platform shapes are measured across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Artifact (probe, verifier, raw reports and certificates): https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/geoar-verifier , under `tacra/`.

Builds cleanly with kramdown-rfc; no new TODOs introduced.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body:
Pushed 31daa0c to keep the binding text in step with the EST profile after Mark's review there (TheBankster/lamps-tacra-est#1):

- The second value of the freshness input now names the RATS Relying Party that relies on the Evidence (the Credential Authority or the Secret Vault), not the credential-acquisition service. Evidence is produced for a Verifier or a Relying Party, never for the CAS. The CAI holds the identifier for the Target or, where a profile allows, takes it from the Initiate result; only a held one makes the Relying Party the intended one.
- The first value is the freshness element of every kind: the Handle, the local epoch identifier, the Attester's timestamp, or nothing for absent-none. The recomputation uses it, and the substitution list notes that freshness that isn't single-use needs the Relying Party identifier to keep Evidence to one Relying Party.

No other change to this PR.
This is "Channel Binding for TLS 1.3"; let's add that string like we did with other RFCs

```suggestion
```

We should not pull such implementation specifica in here. Any objections for removing this?

```suggestion
This is possible whenever the attacker holds the Attester's channel key material, whether leaked, provisioned at runtime, or extracted on another machine: binding Evidence to a public key, with or without a nonce, does not correlate the Evidence with the channel.
```

Rendering this statement an assertion by removing the reference.
Using Attestation Evidence without Authentication in the Open Internet seems to be frowned upon?

CSR + Evidence + Credential Hint would have to be mapped to an issued credential's SAN without any other inputs. To me that sounds like authentication, since the signature by the platform on the Evidence identifies the workload.
It may be problematic for identifying humans on an open internet, but should be sufficient for workloads.
Done — the reference now reads `RFC9266: Channel Binding for TLS 1.3` (in the branch since e20f919).

Agreed — both entries (ID-CRISIS and INTRA-HANDSHAKE-FAIL) are removed, along with their citation in the channel-binding consideration, so the document carries no implementation-specific references. Pushed to the branch.
Applied verbatim; the sentence now stands as an assertion without the citation. Pushed to the branch.

I read both before answering. The IAB statement (Sept 2023) and the liaison to the CCC (Feb 2024) are about *client* attestation used as a barrier to otherwise open services — "adding client attestation into otherwise open systems can significantly reduce openness", and the liaison's worry is basic infrastructure refusing users with non-approved or open-source software. Enrolment here is the other direction: a workload asking its own operator's Credential Authority for a credential, with Evidence describing the platform the CSR was produced on. Nothing about an open service is gated on it, and a client that cannot attest loses nothing it had.

On whether this is authentication, one measured point supports Mark's reading. The platform's signature over Evidence carries an instance identifier the hypervisor did not choose — on SEV-SNP, REPORT_ID, which the firmware generates per guest and keeps for its lifetime (measured across 87 reports from two clouds: one value per instance, none per class). Evidence + CSR bound as in {{binding}} therefore names one workload instance, which is what a SAN needs to be assigned to.

If it helps, I can add one sentence to the security considerations scoping the exchange to workload enrolment and citing the IAB statement, so the concern is answered in the text rather than in this thread.
